title: Post-reset fade and CPU terrain sounds
summary: After an off-track, wreck or manual reset, riders and quads now fade to see-through and back, as in the original, and CPU riders now play the same terrain drive-on sounds and water splashes as the player.
details: Reset fade (#498/#501, closes #485): the rider and quad are drawn at Environment ResetOpacity (default 0.2) for 2 s, ramping back to solid over the last 0.75 s, with no rider-to-rider contact meanwhile. It applies to the player, CPU riders and split-screen players. Lap Attack keeps the player solid and the deep-water reset does not fade. This follows the original USA v2.00 build (001e9050, 001e5260, 001e92c0; research/RACING.md Post-reset fade). Verified by browser tests: in split screen both players fade from 0.2 back to solid; in Lap Attack the player stays solid, also against furyremastered.com. CPU terrain audio (#499, closes #464): CPU riders play the player's drive-on terrain sounds and water splashes, as every quad does in the original (001e33c0 to 002cd6c0). test_engine_cpu_audio requires CPU drive-on voices, on the host and against furyremastered.com. Both changes are live in production at 40b9ce5.
limitation: Training still fades after a wreck (the original skips it); motorcycles and online room riders do not fade; the whole quad fades, including wheels; there is a one-time small hitch on the first fade of a ride while its pipelines compile. CPU water splash is covered by unit tests only; online room guests still hear only CPU engines (#500).
